finding: 2026-09-25 Drew ruling: the unnumbered 2026 Topps baseball Super Box parallel carries ONE spelling, "Silver Crackle Foil". This list folds every row whose destination is FREE onto that canonical address -- one axis (parallel) changed, everything else (sport, year, setKey resolution, cardNumber, isAuto, printRun, player) identical.
rulings: OWNER RULING (Drew, 2026-09-25 ~21:20Z): the unnumbered 2026 Topps baseball Super Box parallel carries ONE spelling, "Silver Crackle Foil". Six spellings of the same unnumbered non-auto rung were measured under setKeys topps / topps-series-1 / topps-series-2 / topps-update / topps-chrome: "Silver Crackle Foil" (~2,720, canonical, untouched), "Silver Crackle Foil (Super Box exclusive)" (1,712 -- a source note leaked into the parallel name), "Silver Crackleboard Foil Board"/"Silver Crackleboard Foil" (measured as "Silver Crackleboard Foil Board" 350 + "Crackleboard Foil" 150 = 500), "Silver Crackle Foilboard" (375), bare "Silver Crackle" (0, none found). Colour rungs (Red/Black/Orange/Gold/Green/Blue/Pink Crackle Foil, numbered) are DISTINCT cards and are excluded by construction -- the census predicate rejects any parallel containing red|black|orange|gold|green|blue|pink|aqua|purple.

SCOPE IS EXACTLY THE RULING'S SIX SPELLINGS, NOT EVERY 'crackle' MATCH. The broader CONTAINS(LOWER(parallel),'crackle') scan over the same predicate also surfaces "Crackle Foil" (332), "Crackle Foil: 10,400 copies" (217), "Crackle Foil: 8700 copies" (217) and bare "Crackle" (50) -- 816 rows total. These carry a PRINT-RUN COUNT inside the parallel string itself (10,400 vs 8,700 copies are different insert-set print sizes) and are not the spelling the ruling names. They are reported to Drew as a separate finding in this PR's body and are NEVER moved or retired by either list -- folding them in would silently merge distinct numbered rungs into one unnumbered pool, which this ruling never authorized.

DESTINATION COMPUTED BY THE REAL computeHobbyIqCardId, NEVER STRING-HACKED. Every destination id in this list was produced by requiring the built dist/services/portfolioiq/hobbyIqCardId.service.js and calling computeHobbyIqCardId with the source row's own sport/year/setKey/cardNumber/isAuto/printRun/playerName, changing ONLY parallel to "Silver Crackle Foil" -- one axis, exactly as the precedent MOVE lists (e.g. 2026-09-07-unseen-forces-unown-question-115.json) require.

topps-series-1 and topps-series-2 rows fold onto a topps-stem destination because resolveSetKeyForSlug (inside computeHobbyIqCardId) canonicalizes the numbered-card rungs of the series-1/series-2 checklists under the parent 'topps' setKey (productSetKeys.ts: topps-series-1/topps-series-2 both declare parent:'topps', refines:'topps') -- the destination id is the function's own output, not an assumption made by this list.

EVERY DESTINATION WAS POINT-READ, at (id, cardId) AND at Cosmos's own None partition key (scripts/lib/catalog-none-pk.cjs resolveNonePk), before bucketing MOVE vs DUPLICATE. Reads only; this census made zero writes.

RESLUG, NOT RETIRE, FOR THIS HALF. Every entry below has a destination that point-read 404 on 2026-09-25 -- these rows are real cards at a non-canonical address, and the fix is to move them, never to delete a card the collision did not create.
MEASURED 2026-09-25: 2461 MOVE entries (topps 358, topps-series-1 2103), sales follow the row (default -- these are NOT a disentanglement, the moved row IS the canonical card).
